_note: Outside-view priors from the two closest prior episodes of debt-financed infrastructure overbuild, for disciplining the verdict tree (src/bubble/verdict_tree.py) and the crack-window timing. Compiled 2026-06-12 from web research; every figure carries a tier. These are ANALOGIES with documented breaks (see analogy_breaks) -- they bound a prior, they do not determine the verdict. Primary cites in analysis/base_rates.md.

telecom_fiber_clec_1998_2003.overbuild_stat: ~2.7% of laid fiber lit in 2002 (WSJ-attributed); ~95%+ dark
telecom_fiber_clec_1998_2003.demand_vs_projection: built for ~7-10x the realized demand curve ('doubling every 100 days' myth vs ~annual doubling)
telecom_fiber_clec_1998_2003.tier: mixed: Moody's default study [agency]; Odlyzko traffic [academic]; WSJ lit-fiber [estimate]

shale_ep_2014_2016.tier: Moody's E&P recovery special comment [agency]; Haynes & Boone monitor [agency-tracker]

capex_peak_to_default_peak_quarters.note: both episodes landed 6-8 quarters despite very different assets; AI capex peak debated, ~2025-2026

equity_peak_to_default_peak_quarters.note: equities rolled over well before realized credit losses peaked

trough_blended_recovery_rate_pct.note: low-20s blended; single-digit cents senior unsecured at the trough

failure_sequence: equity rolls over first (months to ~2yr before realized credit-loss peak)
most-levered, no/negative-cash-flow fringe defaults first (CLECs 2001; high-cost independents 2015)
merchant/overbuild players and fraud-inflated big-caps follow (2002; 2016)
well-capitalized incumbents survive and absorb (RBOCs; oil majors, mostly next cycle)

analogy_breaks.asset_life_is_the_big_one: Fiber had ~20-25yr life and near-zero marginal cost once lit, so the overbuild waited underground and the NEXT cycle's demand absorbed it (dark fiber powered the cloud era). GPUs have ~2-3yr economic life and high power/opex -- AI overbuild DEPRECIATES into obsolescence rather than waiting profitably. The severity prior on PHYSICAL-ASSET recovery should be WORSE-tailed than telecom, even if the timing lag transfers.
analogy_breaks.who_holds_the_debt: Telecom losses sat in public HY bonds + bank/vendor financing (price-transparent, fast to mark). AI leans on private credit, BDCs, insurance/annuity balance sheets, SPV/lease structures, and hyperscaler self-funding -- less price-transparent, slower to mark; could lengthen the lag and dampen the visible default wave.
analogy_breaks.demand_is_real_this_time: Telecom's '100-days' demand curve was fabricated. AI demand is real and growing fast; the open question is price/margin and financing-chain circularity, not whether traffic exists. The break is in KIND: phantom demand vs real demand at possibly-unrecoverable unit economics.
analogy_breaks.shale_trigger_was_exogenous: Shale's bust was triggered by an exogenous commodity-price collapse (OPEC). An AI bust would be ENDOGENOUS (demand/margin/financing disappointment) -- no clean external trigger to time against.
analogy_breaks.incumbent_absorption_rhymes: Hyperscalers (MSFT/GOOG/AMZN/META/NVDA) as deep-balance-sheet incumbents absorbing the levered neocloud fringe is the strongest single transferable pattern -- it matches both episodes' stage 4.
analogy_breaks.split_the_recovery: Do NOT apply one blended recovery number to AI. GPU-specific recovery could be worse than either analog (rapidly depreciating, power-hungry, possibly obsolete); the datacenter shell + power interconnect could recover better (long-lived, supply-constrained).
